meta.description: Identifies essential genes from CRISPR-Cas9 fitness screens using BAGEL2, a Bayesian classifier scoring per-gene Bayes Factors via log-likelihood ratios over per-sgRNA fold changes, calibrated against CEGv2 core-essentials and NEGv1 non-essentials. Covers fc+bf+pr workflow, tumor-suppressor detection, BF calibration, and reproducibility (fixed-seed resampling).

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/p-values/effect sizes in any of the 7 outputs; all numbers traced to real BAGEL2/MAGeCK tool output on real HAP1 TKOv3 data or clearly-labeled synthetic data.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 7 (auditor-authored clinical-decision probe) correctly separates the technical BF interpretation from an individual patient's treatment decision and defers to the clinical pathway; no diagnostic/prescriptive conclusion issued. Flagged as a P2 documentation gap (no explicit disclaimer in the Skill's own text) rather than a veto-firing failure, since the actual output stayed in bounds.

methodological_ground.detail: The prior P0 (interpret_bagel() flagging 86.5% of the genome as tumor-suppressor) is fixed and independently verified: default screen_type='dropout' now returns 0 tumor-suppressor calls and excludes assay-control pseudo-genes; screen_type='enrichment' correctly surfaces TSC1/TSC2 while firing a >5%-flagged sanity warning at the true 86.6% figure.

code_usability.detail: All canonical-path code (BAGEL.py fc/bf/pr, interpret_bagel(), mageck test) ran with real installed tools across all 7 inputs; no syntax errors, no missing dependencies.

functional_suitability.note: fc/bf/pr, tumor-suppressor detection, calibration, MAGeCK/drugZ comparison, and reproducibility are all covered and now internally consistent. Reference-set failure-mode symptoms verified to match documented text for 2 of 3 scenarios (species mismatch, -e/-n swap); the third ('genuinely thin reference -> median BF near zero') was not independently re-verified this pass.

reliability.note: The Common Errors table now documents both the species-mismatch crash and the -e/-n swap silent corruption with actionable fixes, materially improving error reporting/recoverability versus the pre-fix version. The underlying BAGEL.py behavior is unchanged (uncaught traceback / silent NaN column), so this remains documentation-only mitigation, not a code-level guard.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md grew modestly (new Reproducibility section, expanded interpret_bagel(), expanded Common Errors) but remains concise and non-redundant; usage-guide and example script still cleanly separated.

agent_usability.note: All four gaps flagged pre-fix are closed and independently verified: -r flag now documented with correct output schema, and Error Prevention now covers reference-set crash/corruption, non-determinism, and -NB 1000 runtime cost.

human_usability.note: Strict input rejection remains appropriate (Category 3 override, not penalized). Failure symptoms are now pre-announced in the Common Errors table, which meaningfully helps a human/agent recognize them in advance, even though the runtime failure itself is still a raw traceback or silent NaN column.

security.note: No secrets, only public reference-data URLs. Still no pre-flight validation of column names or essential/non-essential reference-gene overlap before running -- the exact gap that let the -e/-n swap corrupt silently remains a code-level gap, mitigated only by documentation.

maintainability.note: Clean separation of SKILL.md/usage-guide/example script and clear CLI parameterization; outputs are now deterministic when the documented -s <int> seed is used (verified byte-identical), resolving the prior Testability gap.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger, good progressive disclosure, clean composability with hit-calling/pathway-analysis Skills. Idempotency is now demonstrated (fixed-seed reruns byte-identical) and escape-hatch/failure-mode guidance now matches independently-verified real tool behavior for the two most common misconfigurations.

key_strengths: Both prior veto conditions are now independently verified fixed: two -s 42 bf reruns produced a byte-identical bayes_factor.txt across all 18,053 genes (T3 determinism), and interpret_bagel() now returns 0 tumor-suppressor calls by default while correctly gating enrichment-mode TS calls behind a >5%-flagged sanity warning (M3 methodological grounding).

Reference-set failure-mode documentation now matches real, independently-reproduced tool behavior for both tested misconfigurations: species-mismatch hard crash and -e/-n swap silent all-NaN corruption (exit 0).
The previously-undocumented -r/--sgrna-bayes-factors flag is now documented with its correct output schema; verified RPS3's 4 per-sgRNA BF values sum exactly to its gene-level BF (66.386 = 66.386).

Cross-tool validation (BAGEL2 vs MAGeCK on the same real HAP1 TKOv3 data) remains strong: Jaccard 0.479, 99.1% of MAGeCK's significant hits recovered, exactly as the Skill's comparison table predicts.

recommendations.title: Reference-set failure modes are documented but not defended by any runtime guard
recommendations.problem: Species mismatch still raises a raw, uncaught Python traceback and the -e/-n swap still writes a fully silent all-NaN bayes_factor.txt with exit 0 -- both symptoms are now accurately described in the Skill's Common Errors table, but a user who does not consult the table in advance gets no runtime signal beyond the documentation.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix addressed documentation accuracy, not the underlying BAGEL.py CLI wrapper -- no pre-flight check validates -e/-n gene-list overlap with the input's GENE column, and no post-run check flags an all-NaN BF column before declaring success.
recommendations.fix: Add a lightweight pre-flight or post-run sanity check to the Skill's example code: verify at least some overlap between -e/-n reference genes and the count file's GENE column before running, and assert the BF column is not >95% NaN after bf completes, printing an explicit warning naming the likely cause (argument swap or species mismatch) rather than relying on the user reading Common Errors.

recommendations.title: No explicit practice-boundary disclaimer despite repeated 'clinical-grade' language
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md and usage-guide.md use 'clinical-grade essentiality calls' / 'clinical-grade' four times (thresholds table, Reproducibility section, Decision Cheat Sheet) with no accompanying caveat that BAGEL2 output from a research screen does not itself constitute a validated clinical assay or support an individual patient treatment decision.
recommendations.root_cause: The phrase was adopted as a stringency label (BF>12 vs BF>6) without considering that an agent following only the Skill's literal text has no textual guardrail against extrapolating it into a real treatment recommendation.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line caveat next to each 'clinical-grade' mention (or a single Practice Boundaries note near the top of SKILL.md) stating that BF thresholds describe statistical stringency within a research screen, not a validated diagnostic or treatment-decision threshold for an individual patient.

recommendations.title: 'Bootstrap CI is wide' Failure Mode symptom did not reproduce under a real thin-coverage test
recommendations.problem: A synthetic 3-sgRNA/gene library (below the Skill's own 4-6/gene recommendation) produced implausibly extreme BF magnitudes under thin coverage, but none of 200 genes showed the literal documented symptom (STD column larger than BF, CI spanning zero) at -NB 1000 -- the entry may overstate how reliably that specific symptom appears versus a more general 'extreme, less trustworthy point estimates' pattern.
recommendations.root_cause: The Failure Mode entry was written from the general statistical expectation (small-sample CI widening) rather than checked against a concrete low-coverage run.
recommendations.fix: Either verify the CI-spans-zero symptom against a low-coverage run with realistic (not exaggerated) effect sizes and adjust the wording accordingly, or broaden the documented symptom to also mention implausibly large BF magnitude as an equally valid red flag for thin per-gene coverage.
